purpose: One customer's orders; the join column o_custkey has no index
sql:
SELECT o.o_orderkey, o.o_orderdate, o.o_totalprice
FROM customer c
JOIN orders o ON o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
WHERE c.c_custkey = 1234

extra.AI Reason: The customer is filtered by a unique key, making a nested loop join with the orders table efficient.
Direct lookup on the primary key of the customer table.
Scanning the orders table to find all orders for the specific customer.

differences.text: PostgreSQL runs part of the plan in parallel (Gather). The AI plan runs in a single process.
Join of (orders, customer): outer and inner inputs are swapped. PostgreSQL's outer input is (orders).
Nested Loop of (orders) with (customer): The AI applies o_custkey = c_custkey here, PostgreSQL does not.

Table customer: PostgreSQL uses Index Only Scan on customer using customer_pkey. The AI uses Index Scan on customer using customer_pkey. A sequential scan wins when many rows qualify. An index scan wins when few rows qualify. A bitmap scan sits in between. The AI's reason: "Direct lookup on the primary key of the customer table."
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Gather over (orders, customer) (collects rows from parallel worker processes).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Materialize over (customer) (stores its input in memory so it can be re-read cheaply).

similarities: Both plans join the tables in the same order (every intermediate join result is the same).
Both plans use Seq Scan on orders.
